unit: one private unweighted undirected hypergraph input (one complete adjacency-hypergraph file)

metrics.name: runtime_seconds
metrics.means: median verifier-measured elapsed seconds of a fresh original-driver process on this hypergraph, including loading, one Compute call, result serialization and process exit; that same execution must return all exact core numbers
metrics.source: verifier parent time.perf_counter_ns brackets execution of the original ligra/ligra.h parallel_main -> Compute -> KCore spine with -rounds 0 and private output observation; no child-reported time or metric is accepted
metrics.clears_when: C_runtime_seconds(w) <= 0.97 * R_runtime_seconds(w), where each quantity is the median of seven verifier-timed fresh-process executions on workload w; candidate and reference execution order alternates between paired repetitions
metrics.tolerance: A fixed 0.03 minimum fractional runtime improvement: C <= (1 - 0.03) * R. This is a stricter beating margin, not additive time slack; equality at 0.97 * R passes.

metrics.name: sequential_runtime_seconds
metrics.means: median verifier-measured elapsed seconds of a fresh original-driver process on this hypergraph with one OpenMP thread (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE), including loading, one Compute call, result serialization and process exit; that same execution must return all exact core numbers. This is the paper's sequential time T1 for work-efficient k-core (Shun, PPoPP 2020, Section 6, Table 3 'T1'), measured on the same retained workloads and binaries as runtime_seconds
metrics.source: judge/evaluator.py _run with threads=SEQUENTIAL_THREADS: the same verifier parent time.perf_counter_ns bracket around the original ligra/ligra.h parallel_main -> Compute -> KCore spine with -rounds 0 and private output observation as runtime_seconds; measured in a separate one-thread pass after the unchanged eight-thread pass; no child-reported time or metric is accepted
metrics.clears_when: C_sequential_runtime_seconds(w) <= 0.97 * R_sequential_runtime_seconds(w), where each quantity is the median of seven verifier-timed fresh-process one-thread executions on workload w; candidate and reference execution order alternates between paired repetitions. A candidate one-thread execution that fails, times out (40 s) or returns any incorrect core number fails this metric for workload w
metrics.tolerance: the same fixed 0.03 minimum fractional improvement as runtime_seconds: C <= (1 - 0.03) * R, a stricter beating margin rather than additive slack; equality at 0.97 * R passes

beats_reference: beats_reference = 1 iff the candidate returns every per-vertex core number exactly equal to the independent oracle on all correctness guards and every timed eight-thread execution, and for every performance workload w in the active suite both C_runtime_seconds(w) <= 0.97 * R_runtime_seconds(w) and C_sequential_runtime_seconds(w) <= 0.97 * R_sequential_runtime_seconds(w), the latter from exact one-thread executions; otherwise beats_reference = 0. A failed, incorrect or unbuildable reference, or an unusable trusted workload, is a failed verification raised to the verifier adapter, never a bar and never a candidate score. Development uses the two feedback workloads. Final independently re-evaluates those two public workloads together with both held-out graded workloads, retaining the full four-workload, two-metric conjunction.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_runtime_seconds_median
solver_feedback.means: the median of the candidate's own runtime_seconds values across the complete development performance suite
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it aggregates only the candidate's absolute elapsed times, is not keyed or ordered by private workload, and contains no reference-derived value

solver_feedback.name: candidate_sequential_runtime_seconds_median
solver_feedback.means: the median of the candidate's own sequential_runtime_seconds values across the complete development performance suite, or null if any one-thread execution failed
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it aggregates only the candidate's absolute one-thread elapsed times, is not keyed or ordered by private workload, and contains no reference-derived value

statement_sentences: In addition to the continuous score, a separate stricter criterion requires all exact core-number checks to pass and, on every final performance workload, covering both public feedback inputs and both held-out graded inputs, both the candidate's seven-run median verifier-measured complete-process runtime with eight threads and its seven-run median runtime with one thread to be at least 3.0% lower than the withheld method's corresponding medians. One incorrect result or one failed workload or metric comparison makes the criterion fail; a correct submission still receives its continuous score, which uses only the eight-thread runtime. Development feedback exposes only candidate-only absolute metrics and aggregate per-metric workload pass/fail counts and percentages. Reference values, individual comparison rows and all final metrics remain private.
comments: Design revision dde8739799944966a4bcfe7a736c0e22, 2026-09-14. Prior authority SHA256 552b0723f62d1030be590363f57e029009564459fdb5fa036dc34035d65133a0 required C<R. For the positive elapsed times enforced by this evaluator, C<=0.97R is strictly stronger. Seven alternating paired executions and exact output validation on every execution preserve the original ligra.h -> Compute -> KCore execution spine and trusted parent timing boundary. Reference restores the exact upstream contribution; the solver surface remains the selected method and frontier_solution helpers. Five raw author development records show a worst absolute paired median ratio difference of 1.6353551573%; the subsequent constrained pipeline preflight passed five development/five final samples and the complete cached model-free oracle path. These are reference validation and measurement evidence, not a genuine solver trial or proof that a solver beats the bar. See the private resume-003 receipts. Reduced retained upstream randHypergraph workloads preserve two distinct strata and separate development/final content hashes; they are narrower than the paper suite. Duplicate-but-distinct hyperedges, singleton edges, isolates, overlaps and cascades remain correctness guards. The sole beating metric remains complete-process runtime, with a conjunction over every selected performance workload. Core numbers remain exact validity guards; memory remains operational evidence. Score 100*exp(-t/0.25), 100 development submissions, 8 CPUs/4096 MiB, eight OpenMP execution threads, 90s compilation, 40s executable and 300s overall evaluation limits remain. The environment startup allowance remains 180s, based on the observed 88.510s cold main-image build plus setup overhead. The T41 production correction changes only Agent/Verifier CPU resources and the equal candidate/reference OpenMP worker count from two to eight; exact workloads, full-process timing, seven repetitions, score, reference and C<=0.97R conjunction are unchanged. The prior 90s failure and two-thread calibration remain historical; no cold 180s replay is claimed. All private identities, rows, reference values, cores and final metrics remain withheld. BEAT SPEC V2 (2026-10-07): adds sequential_runtime_seconds, the paper's Table 3 T1 (one-thread time of the same work-efficient k-core program, the paper's measure of work efficiency next to the parallel T72h), as an independent per-workload metric with the same C <= 0.97R rule, conjoined with the unchanged eight-thread runtime_seconds rule. It is measured by the same trusted parent clock and exact oracle, in a separate one-thread pass after the unchanged eight-thread pass; a candidate one-thread failure fails only that metric, so validity and the continuous score keep their eight-thread definitions. Parallel speedup SU = T1/T72h is not a separate metric because it is a ratio of the two measured times and is improvable by slowing T1; Table 4 stall fraction, LLC miss rate and memory bandwidth need hardware performance counters that the verifier does not expose; Figure 2 thread scaling and Figure 3 size scaling are represented by the two thread counts and the two retained size strata. Reference validity: a failed, incorrect or unbuildable reference, or unusable trusted workloads, now raise a failed verification instead of returning a zero candidate score. Workloads, repetitions, thread count, the 0.97 rule for runtime_seconds, score and budgets are unchanged. FRAMEWORK-FIRST BUILD (2026-10-14): the candidate and reference translation units are compiled with -DHYPER=1 and the original prologue headers hygra.h, index_map.h, bucket.h and edgeMapReduce.h force-included before the editable file, so solver macros cannot rewrite the fixed driver, loader or framework whose time is measured; the measured boundary, workloads, metrics and rules are unchanged. The compiled object may not define any symbol exported by the linked shared libraries (from the linker map, plus the interpreter), except the standard's replaceable allocation functions and COMDAT definitions that the pristine editable file, compiled with the same flags, emits with identical section bytes and relocations, so library code the framework calls cannot be interposed.
